note: Colours the kit deliberately paints differently from the design hand-off. Anything not listed here is drift and fails the check. The hand-off is the authority, so an entry needs a real reason, not just an observation that they differ.

light.muted-foreground.reason: Normal text on the unchanged muted fill #f4f4f5 was 4.392:1 in the historical design. The corrected foreground exceeds WCAG 1.4.3's 4.5:1 floor while retaining its hue. Canonical CSS and RN values move together; test/text-contrast.test.tsx validates all foreground pairs. The historical hand-off is retained as evidence of this intentional accessibility correction.

dark.primary-foreground.reason: Normal text on the unchanged dark primary fill #615fff was 4.384:1. White raises the pair to 4.576:1 without changing the brand fill or standalone accent. Canonical CSS and RN values move together and every pair is guarded by test/text-contrast.test.tsx. This intentionally corrects the historical design's contrast.

dark.warning.reason: One step on the blue channel, at a rounding boundary. The hand-off authors this as oklch(0.769 0.165 70.08); converted at high precision the sRGB blue channel is 9.4506, which rounds to 9, so #f59e09 is the mathematically exact rendering and the kit ships it. Chrome paints 10. The difference is 1/255 on a near-zero channel (about 0.0002 in OKLab, far below perception), and matching a browser's rounding quirk in preference to the exact value would be the wrong correction.
